properties.description: band of three outlined slabs right across the space next to the gallery on Ballu's plan, in line with the bays between the two antechambers; Ballu's text makes this space two rooms, the small room open on the court and another north of it with its own door on the gallery (1916: 177), and the plan draws slabs here rather than a wall, so I've drawn the line between the two rooms as an opening and left it uncertain, since the plan doesn't show what stood on the slabs

properties.building_id: Grande maison au Nord du Capitole

properties.plan_source: Amraoui 2020b: 229, fig. 11.5; Courtois 1951 and Wilson 2001 city plans; round-2 drawing (Oct 2, 2026), set on the wall lines of the imagery

properties.plan_source: Amraoui 2020b: 229, fig. 11.5; Courtois 1951 and Wilson 2001 city plans; round-2 drawing (Oct 2, 2026), set on the wall lines of the imagery

properties.plan_source: Amraoui 2020b: 234, fig. 11.9; round-2 drawing (Sep 29, 2026), set on the wall lines of the imagery
properties.description: narrow opening between rooms 9 and 10, the gap of about seven tenths of a metre that Amraoui leaves between her two sandstone blocks (*harpe en grès*), from tub compartment b into compartment c, with no threshold, and on the ground there's a dark spot in it just west of the wall's line, but Christofle draws solid wall here and it's under a metre wide, so uncertain; if it was a way through, it's the only one between the fullery's two rooms

properties.plan_source: Ballu, Rapport 1923: 43 (plan), 45-46; Ballu, Rapport 1922: 47-53; Germain 1969: 81, fig. 10; round-2 drawing (Oct 3, 2026), set on the wall lines of the imagery
properties.description: break of 0.37 m in the wall between the two north-west rooms, too narrow for a door and most likely a furnace flue, since Ballu puts the hypocausts and their stoking corridor here, so uncertain, and the analysis runs with it closed

properties.plan_source: Ballu, Rapport 1923: 43 (plan), 45-46; Ballu, Rapport 1922: 47-53; Germain 1969: 81, fig. 10; round-2 drawing (Oct 3, 2026), set on the wall lines of the imagery
properties.description: door from the north room east, about 1.2 m. Ballu draws no door into this room, only a stretch about 3 m long in the middle of its east wall drawn as a thin double line, his low or razed wall, and on the ground the wall's light line stops inside that stretch, at about the middle of the room's side, with a dark spot north of it, so the door is put there, but the far side of the gap doesn't show clearly, so uncertain. It opens on ground Ballu leaves blank east of the room, so the room's real way in may have been from the peristyle's north walk instead, where that wall is razed ??

properties.plan_source: Ballu, Rapport 1923: 43 (plan), 45-46; Ballu, Rapport 1922: 47-53; Germain 1969: 81, fig. 10; round-2 drawing (Oct 3, 2026), set on the wall lines of the imagery
properties.description: opening from the big south-west room north into the west room south of the peristyle, about 3.5 m, the gap Ballu's plan leaves at the west end of the big room's north wall, between the corner of its west wall and the end of the long cross wall; on the ground the cross wall's light line runs on through the gap, so either the wall was rebuilt after his time or his plan has the gap wrong ??, uncertain

properties.plan_source: Ballu, Rapport 1923: 43 (plan), 45-46; Ballu, Rapport 1922: 47-53; Germain 1969: 81, fig. 10; round-2 drawing (Oct 3, 2026), set on the wall lines of the imagery
properties.description: opening between the middle and east rooms south of the peristyle, about 2 m, the gap Ballu's plan leaves between the peristyle's south wall and the stub of the wall between the two rooms; on the ground that wall's light line runs on up to the peristyle's south wall, so uncertain

properties.plan_source: Wilson 2001 and Courtois 1951, city plans (not on Ballu 1911a: 74); round-2 drawing (Oct 4, 2026), set on the walls as the imagery shows them
properties.description: an opening onto the cardo in the east wall of the troughs room, which Wilson's city plan (2001) draws about 4 m wide and Courtois's (1951) about 2 m wide at the room's south end, drawn here at Courtois's width; Ballu's plan has the east wall solid there and his text gives the house one entrance, on the south (1911a: 72), Courtois drew it first, where Ballu and Cagnat (1909) have the wall unbroken, and Wilson follows him, so it rests on Courtois alone and the ground doesn't back it, though a cart opening straight into the troughs room would make some sense; it isn't on Ballu's plan at all, only on the city plans of Wilson and Courtois, and the east wall's band runs on unbroken across it as far as it reads, so uncertain, drawn so the question stays on the map

properties.plan_source: Meunier's unpublished 1938 plan of the house, the fragment Germain reproduces (Germain 1969: 122, fig. 17, right), read from Rebuffat's larger reproduction of it (Rebuffat 1974: pl. 'Thamugadi 12'), with Germain's notes on the floors (1969: 125-127, nos 190-192) and Ballu's plan of the complex (Ballu 1911a: 33) for comparison; round-2 drawing (Oct 4, 2026), set on the walls as the imagery shows them
properties.description: the opening with splayed jambs that the croquis draws through the south portico's back wall, out to the corridor it draws south of the house; the south portico's back wall is one of the clearest lines on the ground and its light line runs straight on through here, so the opening rests on the croquis alone and is uncertain

properties.plan_source: Germain 1969: 125-127 (nos 190-192), the room sizes and what the inscription faced; not on Meunier's plan (Germain 1969: 122, fig. 17; Rebuffat 1974: pl. 'Thamugadi 12'); round-2 drawing (Oct 4, 2026)
properties.description: the opening between room 191 and room 192 that Germain's note implies, since one of 191's inscriptions faced the room to the north (1969: 126); not on Meunier's plan and nothing shows on the ground, so uncertain, put in the middle of the partition at a notional width

properties.plan_source: Ballu 1912: 495 (BCTH; offprint p. 33): *quatre boutiques largement ouvertes sur les rues ouest et sud* (four shops wide open onto the west and south streets); where the wall's shadow stops along the room; no plan of this block has them; round-2 drawing (Oct 5, 2026)
properties.description: street door of the narrow west room of the third row; Ballu has four shops in the west half opening wide onto the west and south streets (*quatre boutiques largement ouvertes sur les rues ouest et sud*, four shops wide open onto the west and south streets) but no plan shows their doors, and the room's only about a metre wide inside, so if it's one of them its door can only be about this wide; it sits on the dark patch on the wall line at the room's south end, which isn't a clean break, so uncertain

properties.plan_source: Ballu 1912: 495 (BCTH; offprint p. 33): *quatre boutiques largement ouvertes sur les rues ouest et sud* (four shops wide open onto the west and south streets); where the wall's shadow stops along the room; no plan of this block has them; round-2 drawing (Oct 5, 2026)
properties.description: street door of the big west room of the second row; another of Ballu's shops on the west street, where the wall's light top breaks for about a metre beside a dark hollow on the wall line, but there's a row of dark spots running across the room at the same place, so it may just be something lying across the wall, and no plan has it, so uncertain

properties.plan_source: Ballu 1912: 493 (BCTH; offprint p. 31), *le tout donnant sur le cinquième Decumanus* (all of it opening onto the fifth *decumanus*, the east-west street); placed where the north wall's shadow stops, 1 m wide like the north-street doors of NE.I27 and NE.I21 on Amraoui's plans (Amraoui 2020b: 234, fig. 11.9; 2020a: 134, fig. 4.11); no plan of this block has them; round-2 drawing (Oct 4, 2026)
properties.description: street door of the north-west street room; Ballu says the whole street row gave onto the fifth *decumanus* (*le tout donnant sur le cinquième Decumanus*, all of it opening onto the fifth *decumanus*) but no plan shows the doors, so this one's where the north wall's shadow stops along this room, about 1 m wide like the north-street doors of the blocks next door on Amraoui's plans; the wall's top darkens there too, but it's a guess, so uncertain

properties.plan_source: Ballu 1912: 493 (BCTH; offprint p. 31), *le tout donnant sur le cinquième Decumanus* (all of it opening onto the fifth *decumanus*, the east-west street); placed where the north wall's shadow stops, 1 m wide like the north-street doors of NE.I27 and NE.I21 on Amraoui's plans (Amraoui 2020b: 234, fig. 11.9; 2020a: 134, fig. 4.11); no plan of this block has them; round-2 drawing (Oct 4, 2026)
properties.description: street door of the second street room from the west; on Ballu's word that the row opened onto the street, at the one place along this room where the wall's shadow disappears completely, 1 m like the neighbours' street doors, uncertain since no plan has it

properties.plan_source: Ballu 1912: 493 (BCTH; offprint p. 31), *le tout donnant sur le cinquième Decumanus* (all of it opening onto the fifth *decumanus*, the east-west street); placed where the north wall's shadow stops, 1 m wide like the north-street doors of NE.I27 and NE.I21 on Amraoui's plans (Amraoui 2020b: 234, fig. 11.9; 2020a: 134, fig. 4.11); no plan of this block has them; round-2 drawing (Oct 4, 2026)

properties.plan_source: Ballu 1912: 493 (BCTH; offprint p. 31), *le tout donnant sur le cinquième Decumanus* (all of it opening onto the fifth *decumanus*, the east-west street); placed where the north wall's shadow stops, 1 m wide like the north-street doors of NE.I27 and NE.I21 on Amraoui's plans (Amraoui 2020b: 234, fig. 11.9; 2020a: 134, fig. 4.11); no plan of this block has them; round-2 drawing (Oct 4, 2026)
properties.description: street door of the north-east street room; the last of the row's street doors, where the shadow along the north wall fades in this room; the fourth room, between the third and fourth walls, has no break like this, so it's the one street room without a door, and this one is uncertain like the rest

properties.plan_source: Courtois 1951 city plan and Wilson 2001's plan of Timgad (fig. 12.08, p. 279) for the layout of the block; Ballu 1912: 493 (BCTH; offprint p. 31) for the rooms; walls where the satellite imagery shows them; round-2 drawing (Oct 4, 2026)
properties.description: door from the open space by the central wall through the wall behind the street rooms into the third street room; no plan has a door here, but the wall's shadow stops for about 2 m around the second divider and the top of the wall darkens just east of it, where the door's drawn, and with no plan or text giving the back rooms' doors, the street rooms in front of them are the nearest way to a street; uncertain, a best guess from the ground and the layout

properties.plan_source: Courtois 1951 city plan and Wilson 2001's plan of Timgad (fig. 12.08, p. 279) for the layout of the block; Ballu 1912: 493 (BCTH; offprint p. 31) for the rooms; walls where the satellite imagery shows them; round-2 drawing (Oct 4, 2026)
properties.description: door through the central wall between the big west hall and the fullery room; the central wall's light line goes dark for about half a metre here, one of two such breaks in it (the other is about 2 m further south), and this one is placed nearer the party wall, so a door from the hall into the fullery beside it is the only way into the fullery as drawn; no plan has it, so uncertain

properties.plan_source: Courtois 1951 city plan and Wilson 2001's plan of Timgad (fig. 12.08, p. 279) for the layout of the block; Ballu 1912: 493 (BCTH; offprint p. 31) for the rooms; walls where the satellite imagery shows them; round-2 drawing (Oct 4, 2026)
properties.description: street door of the south-east storeroom on the fourth *decumanus*; the south wall's shadow stops for about a metre near the storeroom's east end, and a vast storeroom (*vaste magasin*) on a street corner might have opened onto the street, the way the storeroom in the ninth house of the sequence (NE.I27) does; Ballu only says the row bordered the fourth *decumanus* and the shadow there is a row of round dark spots, so it's a guess, uncertain

properties.plan_source: Courtois 1951 city plan and Wilson 2001's plan of Timgad (fig. 12.08, p. 279) for the layout of the block; Ballu 1912: 493 (BCTH; offprint p. 31) for the rooms; walls where the satellite imagery shows them; round-2 drawing (Oct 4, 2026)
properties.description: street door of the north-east room of the second row, onto the east street; the room had no way in on the plans, and on the ground the east wall's light top drops out for about half a metre to a metre here, just south of the corner with the wall behind the street rooms, between the bright stretch to the south and the bright patch at the corner, so it reads as a break; rooms on the side streets of the blocks next door open straight onto them, so uncertain, a best guess

properties.plan_source: Courtois 1951 city plan and Wilson 2001's plan of Timgad (fig. 12.08, p. 279) for the layout of the block; Ballu 1912: 493 (BCTH; offprint p. 31) for the rooms; walls where the satellite imagery shows them; round-2 drawing (Oct 4, 2026)
properties.description: second street door of the north-east room of the second row, onto the east street; a second way in from the east street, where the east wall's light top dips again about 2 m up from the party wall; the room's about 5 m along the street, long enough for a workroom to have two doors, but this dip is fainter than the one by the corner and none of the rooms next door that I've drawn has two street doors, so it's the weaker of the two, uncertain

properties.plan_source: Courtois 1951 city plan and Wilson 2001's plan of Timgad (fig. 12.08, p. 279) for the layout of the block; Ballu 1912: 493 (BCTH; offprint p. 31) for the rooms; walls where the satellite imagery shows them; round-2 drawing (Oct 4, 2026)
properties.description: street door of the south-west room, onto the west street; a guess more than a reading, there's a dark spot right on the inside of the west wall here, about 3 m up from the south wall, and that's the clearest sign along the room's two street walls, but the room would otherwise have no way in from a street of its own, so I've put it there, uncertain

properties.plan_source: Courtois 1951 city plan and Wilson 2001's plan of Timgad (fig. 12.08, p. 279) for the layout of the block; Ballu 1912: 493 (BCTH; offprint p. 31) for the rooms; walls where the satellite imagery shows them; round-2 drawing (Oct 4, 2026)
properties.description: door between the south-west room and the room east of it in the south row; no plan has it, but there's a black dot right against the west side of the wall here, about 2 m up from the south wall, the one clear mark along it, so I've read it as the threshold of a doorway between the two rooms, though the wall's faint light line doesn't actually break here; uncertain, since the wall itself only shows on the ground

properties.plan_source: Ballu 1909: 94-95 (BCTH; offprint pp. 22-23, the report on the 1908 excavations) and 1911a (Sept années): 67-68, the rooms as he describes them, with the door where the ground breaks; no plan of this house has its doors; round-2 drawing (Oct 6, 2026)
properties.description: the entrance, on the north street in the axis of the building; Ballu's entrance (*L'entrée est au nord, dans l'axe de l'immeuble*, the entrance is on the north, in the axis of the building, 1911a: 67), opposite the east portico; the north wall's shadow is a little weaker here than anywhere else along the vestibule but it doesn't break, so the door is sure to exist and its place isn't, uncertain

properties.plan_source: Ballu 1909: 94-95 (BCTH; offprint pp. 22-23, the report on the 1908 excavations) and 1911a (Sept années): 67-68, the rooms as he describes them, with the door where the ground breaks; no plan of this house has its doors; round-2 drawing (Oct 6, 2026)
properties.description: street door of the north tiny room; Ballu's two tiny rooms both had openings onto the east street (*possédant des ouvertures sur la rue de l'est*, having openings onto the east street, 1911a: 68); the east wall's shadow is gone for most of a metre here, in line with the room's door from the concrete room, but it's blurry, so uncertain
